Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Governor [[Gretchen Whitmer]] ran for election to a second term, and faced former political commentator [[Tudor Dixon]] in the general election.{{Cite web |last=Mauger |first=Craig |title=Michigan Republican Party calls Tudor Dixon winner of primary race for governor |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2022/08/02/michigan-primary-republican-candidate-governor-dixon-rinke-kelley-soldano-rebrandt/10182001002/ |access-date=2022-08-03 |website=The Detroit News |language=en-US}} Whitmer defeated Dixon by a margin of nearly 11 percentage points, a wider margin than polls indicated as well as a wider margin than Whitmer's first victory [[2018 Michigan gubernatorial election|four years prior]]. Whitmer won independent voters by double-digit margins.{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/10/10/politics/fault-lines-mccarthy-trump-speakership-2024/index.html|title=McCarthy's fall and Trump's rise reflect the same bet among Republicans|publisher=CNN|last1=Brownstein|first1=Ronald|date=October 10, 2023|accessdate=October 10, 2023}} This was the first gubernatorial election in Michigan history in which both major party candidates were women.[https://www.wilx.com/2022/10/13/decision-2022-race-michigan-governor/ Decision 2022: Race for Michigan Governor] [[WILX-TV]] ==Background== ===Process for ballot appearance and fraud allegations=== In order to appear on a primary ballot for the August 2 Democratic and Republican primaries, candidates must submit between 15,000 and 30,000 signatures in addition to their filing paperwork.{{cite news |last1=Jackson |first1=Colin |title=Why several Republican candidates for Michigan governor were blocked from the ballot |url=https://www.npr.org/2022/06/02/1102485484/why-several-republican-candidates-for-michigan-governor-were-blocked-from-the-ba |access-date=9 June 2022 |work=NPR |date=7 June 2022 |language=en}} These signatures are submitted to the Board of State Canvassers, a bipartisan and independent board that verifies petition signatures. Within seven days of the filing deadline, citizens and organizations can challenge nomination signatures submitted by candidates. Voters are only allowed to sign one nomination petition. After the filing deadline, the Board of State Canvassers received nearly 30 challenges to nomination petitions. Among them, the Michigan Democratic Party alleged that several Republican candidates engaged in signature fraud with their petitions. This was followed by a report by the Michigan Bureau of Elections, which alleged that 36 paid signature circulators faked signatures and engaged in practices that added fraudulent signatures to other candidate's petitions. An eight-hour meeting of the Board of State Canvassers reached a deadlock on whether to allow the candidates in question to stay on the ballot. Due to the deadlock, the candidates in question were not allowed to appear on the primary ballot. The rushed pace of the proceedings and the decision were criticized by [[Common Cause]] of Michigan, whose policy director suggested that the candidates in question had to plead their cases to the Board of Canvassers days after finding out about the alleged fraud themselves.{{cite web |last1=Turner |first1=Quentin |title=Common Cause Michigan Comments on Board of State Canvassers Decision to Remove Candidates from Aug. 2 Primary Ballot Common Cause Michigan Issues Statement on Board of State Canvassers Decision to Remove 8 Candidates from Aug. 2 Primary Ballot |url=https://www.commoncause.org/michigan/press-release/cc-michigan-comments-on-bsc-decision-to-remove-candidates-from-ballots/ |publisher=Common Cause Michigan |access-date=9 June 2022 |date=27 May 2022}} Several candidates filed lawsuits appealing the decision. These suits were rejected in the [[Michigan Court of Appeals]].{{cite news |last1=Jackson |first1=Colin |last2=Pluta |first2=Rick |title=Courts deny Craig, Johnson, Markey challenges; uphold removal from primary ballot |url=https://www.michiganradio.org/politics-government/2022-05-31/briefs-filed-in-lawsuit-over-gop-petition-signatures |access-date=9 June 2022 |work=Michigan Public Radio |date=1 June 2022 |language=en}} Three candidates appealed to the [[Michigan Supreme Court]], but these appeals were denied. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== * [[Gretchen Whitmer]], incumbent governor (2019–present) and vice chair of the [[Democratic National Committee]] (2021–present){{cite web|last=Eggert|first=David|date=2021-07-21|title=Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer reelection campaign breaks fundraising record|url=https://www.newsnationnow.com/us-news/midwest/michigan-governor-gretchen-whitmer-raises-8-5m-for-reelection-campaign-in-7-months/|access-date=2021-08-02|website=News Nation|language=en-US}} ** Running mate: [[Garlin Gilchrist]], incumbent lieutenant governor (2019–present) ===Endorsements=== {{Endorsements box | title= Gretchen Whitmer | list= '''Organizations''' *[[314 Action]]{{cite web|date=June 29, 2021|title=314 Action Fund Endorses Michigan Ticket of Gov. At the filing deadline, 10 candidates submitted enough signatures to appear on the ballot, a state record. However, following challenges by the state Democratic party and other organizations, five candidates were deemed ineligible to appear on the ballot due to alleged fraudulent signatures. Several of these candidates, including former Detroit police chief [[James Craig (police chief)|James Craig]] and Michael Markey, pledged to appeal the decision to the State Supreme Court. Craig also mentioned that, should the appeal fail, he would still plan to run as a [[write-in candidate]] for both the primary and the general election. On June 15, 2022, Craig announced he was launching a write-in campaign for the nomination.{{cite web |url=https://detroit.cbslocal.com/2022/06/15/james-craig-files-as-write-in-for-michigan-gop-governor-primary/ |title=James Craig Files As Write-In For Michigan GOP Governor Primary|date=June 15, 2022 }} On June 9, 2022, candidate Ryan Kelley was arrested by the [[FBI]] following numerous tips that he had participated in the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack]].{{cite news |last1=Pluta |first1=Rick |title=Michigan candidate for governor, Ryan Kelley, arrested by FBI for Jan. 6 involvement |url=https://www.npr.org/2022/06/09/1103925150/michigan-candidate-for-governor-ryan-kelley-arrested-by-fbi-for-jan-6-involvemen |access-date=9 June 2022 |work=NPR |date=9 June 2022 |language=en}} The criminal complaint alleges that Kelley engaged in disorderly conduct on restricted grounds and engaged in acts of violence against a person or property. Most Republican donors chose not to fund campaign ads for Dixon, causing the TV airwaves to be dominated by ads for Whitmer, which included negative ads against Dixon.{{cite web | url=https://www.freep.com/story/news/politics/elections/2022/11/10/mich-gop-memo-gives-scathing-post-mortem-on-trump-backed-candidates/69638845007/ | title=Michigan GOP memo delivers scathing election post-mortem on Trump-backed candidates }} Whitmer also spent a lot more in digital advertising compared to Dixon.{{Cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/news/politics/elections/2023/01/01/whitmer-campaign-spending-facebook-youtube/69766165007/|title=Records: Whitmer amped up Facebook and YouTube ads in 2022 campaign|website=Detroit Free Press|accessdate=March 11, 2023}} Abortion rights, [[2022 Michigan Proposal 3|which were on the ballot in the same election]], were the subject of negative ads against Dixon, who opposed abortion rights.{{cite web | url=https://www.nysun.com/article/for-a-swing-state-michigans-gubernatorial-race-looks-like-lost-cause-for-gop | title=In Michigan, a Swing State, Gubernatorial Race Looks Like Lost Cause for GOP | date=September 23, 2022 }} Although aggregate polling had Whitmer up by about 3%, and a last-minute poll by [[Trafalgar Group]] had Dixon ahead by 1%, the election was not close. Whitmer defeated Dixon at the same time Michigan voters approved a ballot measure that would guarantee abortion rights in the Michigan constitution.{{cite web | url=https://www.theoaklandpress.com/2022/11/08/whitmer-nessel-benson-winning-re-election-in-oakland-county-and-statewide/ | title=Whitmer, Nessel, Benson winning re-election in Oakland County and statewide | date=November 9, 2022 }} Democrats swept the other statewide partisan races and won control of both the [[Michigan House of Representatives|state House]] and [[Michigan Senate|state Senate]].{{cite web | url=https://www.mlive.com/politics/2022/11/michigan-senate-goes-dem-for-first-time-in-4-decades-with-the-aid-of-redistricting-abortion.html | title=Michigan Senate goes dem for first time in 4 decades with the aid of redistricting, abortion | date=November 9, 2022 }} This marked the first time Democrats took control of both houses of the Michigan legislature since 1984.{{cite web | url=https://www.mlive.com/politics/2022/11/michigan-sees-democratic-domination-after-party-sweeps-state-legislative-and-federal-contests.html | title=Michigan sees Democratic domination after party sweeps state, legislative and federal contests | date=November 11, 2022 }} Exit polls found that Whitmer won nearly 70% of college-educated White women and 94% of Black voters.{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/09/17/politics/blue-wall-states-harris-trump-analysis/index.html|title=Why these three states are the most consistent tipping point in American politics|publisher=CNN|last=Brownstein|first=Ronald|date=September 16, 2024|accessdate=September 16, 2024}} This was the first election since [[1990 Michigan gubernatorial election|1990]] in which the winner was from the same party as the incumbent president, and the first time that the incumbent was a Democrat since [[1950 Michigan gubernatorial election|1950]].{{cite web | url=https://www.sbam.org/mi-elected-governor-of-same-party-as-sitting-president-4-times-in-last-22-mid-terms/ | title=MI Elected Governor of Same Party as Sitting President 4 Times in Last 22 Mid-Terms | date=October 11, 2022 }} Despite Dixon's loss, she managed to flip [[Gogebic County, Michigan|Gogebic County]] in the Upper Peninsula (which last voted for a Republican in 1998), making this the first election since [[1932 Michigan gubernatorial election|1932]] where a Democrat won the Michigan governor's mansion without carrying Gogebic County.{{cite web | url=https://www.detroitchamber.com/twig-2022-11-11/ | title=Nov. 11, 2022 | This Week in Government: Whitmer Wins Reelection; Dixon Concedes | date=November 11, 2022 }} Conversely, Whitmer flipped the counties of [[Benzie County, Michigan|Benzie]] and [[Grand Traverse County, Michigan|Grand Traverse]]; the last time the Democratic candidate won these counties were [[2006 Michigan gubernatorial
